description:
Cam Ward captured the 2006 Conn Smythe Trophy as Stanley Cup Playoffs MVP, backstopping the Carolina Hurricanes to the first championship in franchise history. The rookie goaltender delivered one poised, pressure-packed performance after another, announcing himself on the game’s biggest stage.
In the opening round against Montreal, Carolina stumbled out of the gate, dropping the first two games at home and heading on the road facing a crucial Game 3. Ward answered the call, turning aside chance after chance and steering the Hurricanes to an overtime victory. Among his many stops was a stunning point-blank glove save from the slot that helped preserve Carolina’s season.
Ward’s brilliance continued in the Stanley Cup Final against Edmonton, where he was once again tested throughout a seven-game battle. In Game 1, he dazzled the crowd with multiple glove saves in the third period, including a spectacular stop in the final seconds to protect a one-goal lead. Then in Game 7, with everything on the line and Carolina clinging to that same slim margin late in the third, Ward stretched out his pad to deny another sure goal.
By the end of the postseason, Ward had cemented his legacy, posting a .920 save percentage and a 2.14 goals-against average, and delivering one of the most remarkable rookie playoff runs in NHL history.

description:
Victor Hedman authored one of the most dominant postseason performances by a defenseman in NHL history during Tampa Bay’s 2020 Stanley Cup run. Recording 10 goals and 12 assists for 22 points in 25 games while logging over 26 minutes per night, Hedman’s offensive production and all-situations dominance were pivotal in capturing the Conn Smythe Trophy. His 10 goals stand as the third-most ever by a defenseman in a single postseason, underscoring the historic nature of his run.  
In the opening sequence, Hedman clinches the series against Boston in Game 5 of the Second Round, receiving a pass and firing a shot through traffic that beats the goaltender in double overtime. 
He follows that up in the Eastern Conference Final with a display of elite vision, threading a precise feed to Brayden Point, who redirects it home in Game 1 against the Islanders.  
In the final sequence, Hedman once again comes through in a critical moment, scoring the game-winning goal in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final versus Dallas—giving Tampa Bay its first lead of the series and setting the tone for a championship they would secure in six games.

description:
Ryan O’Reilly’s Conn Smythe-winning performance in 2019 powered the St. Louis Blues to their first Stanley Cup in franchise history, as his elite two-way play, relentless compete level, and clutch scoring defined the team’s postseason run. Tying a franchise record with 23 points, O’Reilly consistently delivered in the biggest moments while anchoring the Blues in all situations.  
In the opening sequence, St. Louis faces a daunting 2-0 deficit early in the third period of a pivotal Game 5 in Winnipeg with the series tied 2-2. On the power play, O’Reilly battles to the front of the net and buries a rebound, igniting a comeback that shifts the series in the Blues’ favor. 
He rises to the occasion again in Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final against Boston, with St. Louis trailing in the series. In a tied game midway through the third, O’Reilly drives the crease and cashes in on another rebound for the game-winning goal—his second of the night in a statement performance.  
In the final sequence, O’Reilly showcases his timing and net-front presence once more, finding open ice at the top of the crease and converting on a perfectly placed pass to open the scoring in Game 5 of the Final. He later adds an assist in the Blues’ 2-1 victory, giving St. Louis its first series lead—one they would not relinquish en route to a historic Game 7 triumph.

description:
Justin Williams earned the 2014 Conn Smythe Trophy as Stanley Cup Playoffs MVP, leading the Los Angeles Kings to their second championship in three seasons. Known for his clutch performances, Williams consistently delivered in the biggest moments, pairing timely scoring with steady leadership throughout the postseason.
In the opening round against in-state rival San Jose Sharks, Williams played a pivotal role in one of the most remarkable comebacks in playoff history. With the Kings trailing the series three games to none, he scored twice in a must-win Game 6, including the go-ahead and eventual game-winning goal midway through the third period, helping propel Los Angeles to a seven-game series victory.
Williams continued his heroics in the Second Round against another California rival, the Anaheim Ducks. In Game 7, he opened the scoring, giving the Kings a lead they would never surrender. Then in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final versus the New York Rangers, Williams came through once more, scoring the overtime winner to give Los Angeles a series lead it would not relinquish, ultimately capturing the Cup in five games and securing the third Stanley Cup championship of his career.

description:
Evgeni Malkin captured the 2009 Conn Smythe Trophy as the Stanley Cup Playoffs MVP, powering the Pittsburgh Penguins to their first championship since 1992. A dominant presence throughout the postseason, Malkin led all players in scoring, blending elite skill, strength, and creativity to overwhelm opponents and seize control of games when it mattered most.
His most commanding performance came in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Final against the Carolina Hurricanes. After scoring in the first period, Malkin took over in the third, netting the go-ahead goal midway through the frame before dazzling with a spectacular backhand tally just minutes later to put the game out of reach. The four-point night—three goals and an assist, to go along with eight shots—stood as one of the defining performances of the playoffs.
Malkin finished the postseason with a playoff-best 36 points, cementing his place as the driving force behind Pittsburgh’s championship run.

description:
Duncan Keith’s 2015 Conn Smythe Trophy run was a defining force behind Chicago’s third Stanley Cup in six seasons, as the veteran blueliner delivered elite two-way play, huge minutes, and timely offense at every stage of the postseason. In the opening sequence, Keith seals the first-round series against Nashville in Game 6, striking with less than four minutes remaining in the third period to send the Blackhawks through. He rises to the occasion again in the Western Conference Final against Anaheim, with Chicago facing elimination in Game 6, recording three assists in a clutch win to force a Game 7. The standout moment of that performance is his brilliant setup to Marian Hossa, a play that captures Keith’s vision and composure under pressure. Then, in the final sequence, Keith puts the finishing touch on a championship run for the ages by scoring the Stanley Cup-clinching goal in Game 6 against Tampa Bay.
